Evan Huang is associated with a personal project called **Camazotz**, a handheld device designed for real-time underwater cave mapping and navigation. This project also involves the design and sale of other cave diving equipment. The device utilizes RP2350 firmware for live "stick map" rendering, integrating data from an encoder, an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), and a depth sensor. Beyond Camazotz, Evan Huang's interests include distributed systems and developer tooling. He is also recognized as a RISE Global Winner and VEX Robotics Challenge World Winner for his "DrinkBot" invention, which aims to enhance the quality of life for the elderly and disabled.

It is important to note that there is also a researcher named **Yewei Huang** whose work is related to underwater mapping. Yewei Huang, a Mechanical Engineering Ph.D. graduate (2025), conducts research on multi-robot systems and the application of underwater navigation to larger robot teams and swarms. Her work addresses significant challenges in underwater robotics, including communication, navigation, and perception, which are often compromised underwater. She is also a co-author on a preprint titled "Underwater Dense Mapping with the First Compact 3D Sonar," developed within Ioannis M. Rekleitis's lab at the University of Delaware. This research explores the use of compact 3D sonar for detailed reconstructions and localization in underwater cave systems and other geometrically and acoustically challenging environments.

results.response_text:
Several individuals and initiatives are actively building DIY and open-source hardware for underwater and cave mapping.

**Phil Underwood** has been a significant figure in developing open-source hardware for cave surveying. His project has evolved from basic electronic surveying tools to a Raspberry Pi-based system capable of generating textured 3D models of underground environments. His work aims to make underground surveying faster and the equipment practical to build and modify.

**Addison Snyder** is another individual actively working on DIY underwater cave mapping hardware. Snyder is developing a self-contained LiDAR setup specifically designed for use in underwater caves and has shared progress on the Blue Robotics Community Forums.

While not exclusively focused on "DIY underwater cave mapping hardware," other open-source projects and research contribute significantly to the broader field of underwater mapping:
*   Researchers at the **University of Minnesota** are developing MeCO, an open-source Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) platform with modular sensors for identifying and tracking invasive species in freshwater lakes. The Camazotz cave mapping project refers to the development of an integrated underwater cave mapping system and associated software by Camazotz Diving. This project aims to transform exploration dives into detailed 3D maps in real time.

Key features and components of the Camazotz Cave Mapper System include:
*   **Real-time Mapping** The system combines multiple sensor inputs to build a real-time model of the cave passage as a diver swims.
*   **Sensor Integration** It utilizes a high-precision depth sensor, a magnetic encoder for distance measurement by tracking line deployment, and a 9-axis inertial measurement unit (IMU) for heading and attitude.
*   **Data Processing** A dual-core processor records and combines sensor data 100 times per second to plot the diver's position, resulting in a real-time "stick map".
*   **Post-Dive Analysis** After a dive, the software can generate 2D passage profiles (plan and cross-section views), 3D point cloud visualizations, and export data to standard cave survey formats like Compass and Walls.
*   **Browser-based Software** Camazotz Diving also offers free, browser-based cave mapping software for visualizing 3D cave surveys, which can work offline.

The Camazotz Cave Mapper System is currently in active development and field testing. It is a custom-built tool designed for cave divers to create accurate maps of underwater cave systems.

The Camazotz Cave Mapper System is a high-tech, fully integrated underwater cave mapping solution developed by Camazotz Diving .
Designed "by divers, for divers," it is engineered to turn challenging overhead exploration dives into detailed 3D maps and models without the need for manual, traditional data-logging underwater.
The system mounts onto a diver's gear and utilizes a dual-core processor to combine multiple sensor inputs 100 times per second, plotting an accurate "stick map" of the path in real time:
Depth Profiling: Uses a high-precision pressure transducer to measure accurate depth.
Distance Tracking: Measures the exact distance of a dive using a magnetic encoder coupled directly to the deployment of the guideline wheel.
Heading and Attitude: Employs a 9-axis inertial measurement unit (IMU) and compass to capture the exact directional changes and angles of the cave passages.
After a dive, the captured data log is connected to a computer. Using Camazotz Diving's browser-based tools (which process data locally using WebAssembly for privacy and offline functionality), it generates:
2D passage profiles (both plan and cross-section views).
3D point cloud visualizations of the underwater cave network.
Exportable data files compatible with industry-standard cave survey software like Walls or .
